system.name: Plaid
system.one_liner: a CGRA architecture and compiler that aligns compute and communication resources by exploiting recurring dataflow-graph motifs

components.name: LD
components.role: load node in the dataflow graph; part of a motif executed on the collective unit

components.name: ST
components.role: store node in the dataflow graph, executed on the ALSU

components.name: motifs
components.role: dashed outlines marking recurring three-node communication patterns identified by Plaid's compiler

components.name: Plaid Collective Unit (PCU)
components.role: per-tile compute unit that executes a full three-node motif and routes its data dependencies together

components.name: ALU
components.role: 16-bit compute unit supporting ADD, MUL, SHIFT and bit-wise operations (15 ops total); three per PCU

components.name: ALSU
components.role: additional arithmetic/load-store unit in the PCU

components.name: Local Router (8x8)
components.role: delivers inputs to and collects outputs from the three ALUs each cycle, with virtual bypass paths between ALUs to shorten routing

components.name: Global Router (7x9)
components.role: connects the PCU to neighboring tiles via N/S/E/W ports, with optional register buffering on the datapath

flows.what: motif nodes mapped onto PCU compute and routing resources

content.key_idea: A dataflow graph decomposes into recurring three-node motifs; Plaid's Collective Processing Unit executes a whole motif at once via ALUs tightly coupled to a local router.

summary: Plaid is a CGRA architecture and compiler that aligns compute and communication resources by identifying recurring three-node communication patterns, called motifs, in an application's dataflow graph. This three-panel figure connects that idea to hardware: panel (a) shows a hierarchical dataflow graph with LD, arithmetic, and ST nodes, where dashed outlines group nodes into motifs, and red leader lines annotate which hardware resource (global router, three ALUs, local router/bypass path, ALSU) executes each part. Panel (b) shows the Plaid architecture as a grid of tiles connected by a 16-bit global-router interconnect. Panel (c) zooms into one Plaid Collective Unit (PCU), the tile's core: three blue ALUs and an ALSU surround a local router (8x8) that feeds and collects their operands every cycle, and a global router (7x9) links the tile to its north/south/east/west neighbors, with a CONFIG input controlling the unit's behavior.
summary_zh: 该图分三部分展示Plaid：(a)数据流图中虚线圈出三节点通信模体，红色引线标注对应硬件；(b)瓦片阵列构成的Plaid架构；(c)放大的PCU，三个ALU与ALSU围绕本地路由器，经全局路由器连相邻瓦片。
